categories.title: Slurry, manure and agricultural effluent management (ssafo-nitrates)
categories.description: Slurry, manure, and agricultural effluent management covering storage, spreading, and disposal of livestock waste including pig slurry, poultry manure, farmyard manure (FYM), liquid manure, silage effluent, and digestate. Covers storage infrastructure requirements such as slurry tanks, lagoons, slurry stores, reception pits, lined lagoons, freeboard, structural integrity, and secondary containment. Includes land application controls covering application rates, buffer zones, closed periods, and muck spreading. Covers environmental protection requirements including ammonia emissions, runoff prevention.

An application for derogation must be submitted between 1st October and 31st December in the calendar year preceding the calendar year to which the application relates.

Storage facilities are not necessary for slurry or poultry manure that the occupier intends will be sent off the holding.

The base of a silo must have adequate provision for the drainage of silage effluent from the perimeter channels to an effluent tank through a channel or pipe.
The record of nitrogen produced by animals on the holding must include the number of days that each animal spent on the holding.
Where the walls of a slurry storage tank are not impermeable, the base of the tank must be provided with channels designed and constructed so as to collect any slurry that escapes from the tank.

The review of the action programme must include the considerations upon which decisions are based, including public participation.

When determining restrictions on spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the weather conditions must be taken into account.

Livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure) must not be spread directly onto surface water.
A record of livestock manure brought on to the holding must include the date on which it was brought on to the holding.
A record must be kept of the date on which livestock manure was sent off the holding.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer must follow the rules for storing silage, slurry or agricultural fuel oil.
source_paragraphs: You must follow these rules if you store silage, slurry or agricultural fuel oil.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A land manager must follow the rules for storing silage, slurry or agricultural fuel oil.
source_paragraphs:
You must make sure you meet the rules if you're a:
farmer
land manager
tenant farmer – unless you can prove someone else, for example the leaseholder, is jointly or wholly responsible

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A tenant farmer must follow the rules for storing silage, slurry or agricultural fuel oil unless they can prove someone else, for example the leaseholder, is jointly or wholly responsible.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A person who does not follow the rules or take care to avoid causing pollution can be prosecuted and fined up to £5,000 in a magistrates' court, or receive an unlimited fine in the Crown Court.
source_paragraphs: If you do not follow the rules or take care to avoid causing pollution you can be prosecuted and fined up to £5,000 in a magistrates' court, or get an unlimited fine in the Crown Court.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A new or substantially changed store must follow the specific rules for the substance being stored.
source_paragraphs:
A new or substantially changed store must:
follow the specific rules for the substance you're storing
have an expected lifespan of at least 20 years with maintenance – any part of a silage effluent tank that's underground must last 20 years without maintenance
be at least 10 metres clear of inland or coastal waters – you may need a larger safety zone in some cases, for example near a water supply intake

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A new or substantially changed store must have an expected lifespan of at least 20 years with maintenance; any part of a silage effluent tank that is underground must last 20 years without maintenance.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: An installation built before March 1991, or where a construction contract was entered into before March 1991 and completed before September 1991, is exempt from the rules for new stores.
source_paragraphs: If your installation was built before March 1991, or a contract for construction was entered into before March 1991 and completed before September 1991, it's exempt from the rules for new stores. However, if you make substantial changes, for example structural changes, increasing capacity or relocating your store, it is no longer exempt.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: An installation built before March 1991 that is subject to substantial changes — for example structural changes, increasing capacity or relocating the store — is no longer exempt from the rules for new stores.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: The Environment Agency may at any time serve a notice requiring a farmer to bring storage up to current standards if it believes there is a significant risk of pollution.
source_paragraphs: The Environment Agency can also serve a notice at any time requiring you to bring storage up to the current standards if it believes there's a significant risk of pollution.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer must notify the Environment Agency at least 14 days before beginning construction of a new or substantially changed store for silage, slurry or agricultural fuel oil.
source_paragraphs: notify the Environment Agency at least 14 days before you begin construction – you can also contact them for advice on planning and building a store

You must notify the Environment Agency at least 14 days before you:
build new storage for silage, slurry or agricultural fuel oil, or make substantial changes to an existing store
store field silage on a new site

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer must not pollute the surrounding environment — for example rivers or other watercourses — when constructing storage.
source_paragraphs: make sure you do not pollute the surrounding environment – for example rivers or other watercourses

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: Once storage is built, a farmer must carry out maintenance to make sure there is no risk of pollution.
source_paragraphs: Once your storage is built you must carry out maintenance to make sure there's no risk of pollution.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer must notify the Environment Agency at least 14 days before storing field silage on a new site.

You must notify the Environment Agency at least 14 days before you:
build new storage for silage, slurry or agricultural fuel oil, or make substantial changes to an existing store
store field silage on a new site

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: The rules for storing silage do not apply to silage stored temporarily in a container or trailer for transportation.
source_paragraphs: The rules do not apply to silage you store temporarily in a container or trailer for transportation.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer must not make or store any silage, or unwrap baled silage, within 10 metres of inland or coastal waters.
source_paragraphs: You must not make or store any silage, or unwrap baled silage within 10 metres of inland or coastal waters.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer must not store field silage within 50 metres of a protected water supply source.
source_paragraphs: In addition, you must not store field silage within 50 metres of a protected water supply source.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A protected water supply source is any place where water is abstracted for human consumption, use in farm dairies, or human food preparation.
source_paragraphs:
In addition, you must not store field silage within 50 metres of a protected water supply source. This is any place where water is abstracted (taken) for any of the following purposes:
human consumption
use in farm dairies
human food preparation

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: All parts of a silo must be resistant to attack.
source_paragraphs: All parts of a silo must be resistant to attack.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A silo must have an impermeable base extending beyond any walls.
source_paragraphs:
Your silo must have:
an impermeable base extending beyond any walls
impermeable drainage collection channels around the outside, flowing into an effluent tank

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A silo must have impermeable drainage collection channels around the outside, flowing into an effluent tank.

British Standard 8007:1987 and British Standard 8110-1:1997 (for concrete bases)

source_paragraphs: If your silo has walls, they must withstand wall loadings set in British Standard 5502-22:2003+A1:2013.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A silo must have an effluent collection system.
source_paragraphs: Your silo must have an effluent collection system.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: If all parts of an effluent tank are above ground, the tank must be constructed to resist attack from silage effluent for at least 20 years with maintenance.
source_paragraphs: If all parts of an effluent tank are above ground the tank must be constructed to resist attack from silage effluent for at least 20 years with maintenance. If any part is below ground it should be impermeable for at least 20 years without maintenance.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: If any part of an effluent tank is below ground, it should be impermeable for at least 20 years without maintenance.
source_paragraphs: If all parts of an effluent tank are above ground the tank must be constructed to resist attack from silage effluent for at least 20 years with maintenance. If any part is below ground it should be impermeable for at least 20 years without maintenance.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer must never put silage effluent into an under-floor slurry store.
source_paragraphs: you must never put silage effluent into an under-floor slurry store.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer must seal baled silage in an impermeable membrane or bag.
source_paragraphs: You must seal baled silage in an impermeable membrane or bag. It does not need a specially constructed base but you must make sure any silage stored directly on the ground cannot leak into a water source.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer must make sure any baled silage stored directly on the ground cannot leak into a water source.
source_paragraphs: You must seal baled silage in an impermeable membrane or bag. It does not need a specially constructed base but you must make sure any silage stored directly on the ground cannot leak into a water source.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer must keep baled silage at least 10 metres clear of inland or coastal waters.
source_paragraphs: You must keep baled silage at least 10 metres clear of inland or coastal waters.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: For silage to be stored as field silage, there must be no construction works such as walls or earth banks, and topsoil must not be disturbed.
source_paragraphs: For silage to be stored as field silage there must be no construction works, for example walls or earth banks. Also, topsoil must not be disturbed.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer making field silage or non-baled bags must choose a suitable site and ensure any drainage can be contained.
source_paragraphs:
If you make field silage or non-baled bags, you must:
choose a suitable site – for example if you store silage in a non-baled bag in your farmyard, you must make sure you can contain any drainage
notify your local Environment Agency office at least 14 days before you first use the site

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer making field silage or non-baled bags must notify the local Environment Agency office at least 14 days before first using the site.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: Slurry run-off from solid manure stores, woodchip, straw-bedded corrals and stand-off pads must be collected and stored either separately or in the main slurry store.
source_paragraphs: You must collect and store it either separately or in your main slurry store. This does not apply to slurry you store temporarily in a container or trailer for transportation.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer must not place slurry storage tanks, effluent tanks, channels or reception pits within 10 metres of inland or coastal waters without written agreement from the Environment Agency.
source_paragraphs: You must not put slurry storage tanks, effluent tanks, channels or reception pits within 10 metres of inland or coastal waters without written agreement from the Environment Agency.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: Slurry tanks, reception pits, pipes and channels must be impermeable and meet the anti-corrosion standards set in British Standard 5502-50:1993+A2:2010.

source_paragraphs: You'll normally need capacity for at least 4 months' slurry storage.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: Temporary slurry storage facilities such as a reception pit must be large enough to store a minimum of 2 days' combined slurry production and likely rainfall.
source_paragraphs: Any temporary storage facilities you have – such as a reception pit – must be large enough to store a minimum of 2 days' combined slurry production and likely rainfall.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: If a slurry tank, effluent tank or reception pit is fitted with a drainage pipe, it must have 2 valves separated by at least 1 metre.
source_paragraphs: If your slurry tank, effluent tank or reception pit is fitted with a drainage pipe it must have 2 valves separated by a least 1 metre. Each valve must be able to shut off the flow of slurry and be locked when not in use.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: An earth-banked slurry store must have impermeable soil to a thickness of at least 1 metre.
source_paragraphs: An earth-banked store must have impermeable soil to a thickness of at least 1 metre. You may need laboratory analysis and confirmation from a civil engineer to be sure your soil is suitable. Alternatively, you can import impermeable soil or use a synthetic liner.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: The permeability of compacted soil in an earth-banked slurry store must be less than 1 x 10⁻⁹ metres per second (0.000001 mm per second), tested to BS 1377-6:1990 or BS EN 1997-2:2007.
source_paragraphs: The permeability of your compacted soil must be less than 1 x 10 -9 metres per second (0.000001 mm per second). Testing should be to BS 1377-6:1990 or to BS EN 1997-2:2007.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: The base of a weeping-wall slurry store must extend beyond its walls and include perimeter drains to catch escaped slurry and drain into an effluent tank.
source_paragraphs: The base of a weeping-wall store must extend beyond its walls and include perimeter drains to catch escaped slurry and drain into an effluent tank.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: An irrigation system must not deposit slurry within 10 metres of inland freshwater or 50 metres of any water supply.
source_paragraphs: Your irrigation system must not deposit slurry within 10 metres of inland freshwater or 50 metres of any water supply.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer must assess the risk of direct run-off from land intended to be irrigated with slurry and identify unsuitable areas.
source_paragraphs: You must assess the risk of direct run-off from land you intend to irrigate, and identify unsuitable areas.

You must follow these rules if you both:

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: A farmer is responsible for taking precautions to prevent and contain spillages wherever fuel oil is stored on their land.
source_paragraphs: Wherever fuel oil is stored on your land you're responsible for taking precautions to prevent and contain spillages – for example by fitting an alarm to alert you to overfilling.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: Agricultural fuel oil must be stored in a tank or drum that meets ISO 9000.
source_paragraphs: You can store fuel oil in one location or spread across your farm. It must be stored in a tank or drum that meets ISO 9000.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: No part of an agricultural fuel oil installation can be within 10 metres of inland or coastal waters, including yard drains, dry ditches and land drains.
source_paragraphs: No part of your installation can be within 10 metres of inland or coastal waters – including yard drains, dry ditches and land drains.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: Underground agricultural fuel oil tanks must follow the Defra groundwater protection code.
source_paragraphs: If tanks are underground, they must also follow the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra) groundwater protection code.

guidance_propositions.proposition_text: An agricultural fuel oil tank or drum must be surrounded by a secondary containment structure or bund.
source_paragraphs: A tank or drum must be surrounded by a secondary containment structure or bund.
